post.title: Why You Stop Checking Your Bank App When It's Bad #shorts
post.description: Which app do you avoid opening? Tell me in the comments. Send this to the friend with 300 unread emails. Nia's bank app pings after a bad week, and she flips her phone face down. In 'The Ostrich Effect: Selective Attention to Information' (Journal of Risk and Uncertainty, 2009), Niklas Karlsson, George Loewenstein and Duane Seppi looked at how often real investors (Swedish pension savers and US Vanguard clients) logged in to check their accounts. They looked up their portfolios more often when the market was rising and less often when it was flat or falling. Bad news stings, so we dodge it, even though the facts stay the same. It's called the ostrich effect. Fun part: real ostriches don't bury their heads in the sand; the authors point out it's a myth. #psychology #shorts #ostricheffect #overthinking #money
